proofs.proof_tex:
Fix \(n\), abbreviate \(t=t_{J_n,P}\), \(G=G_{J_n,P}=E_P[tt^{\prime}]\), and \(g=g_{\Delta,J_n,P}\), and write \(D=D\Delta_{\mathrm{cmp},P}\).  Lemma \(\ref{lem:complete-normal-tangent-projection}\), applied separately to every coordinate of the declared dictionary, gives
\[
t_j=\Pi_{\mathcal T_P}\{v_j-E_P[v_j]\}\in\mathcal T_P
\qquad (j=1,\ldots,J_n).
\tag{1}
\]
Because \(\mathcal T_P\) is a linear subspace, (1) implies
\[
\mathcal S_{J_n,P}=\{c^{\prime}t:c\in\mathbb R^{J_n}\}\subseteq\mathcal T_P.
\tag{2}
\]

We next verify the range condition required by the Moore--Penrose formula; it is not imposed as an assumption.  If \(c\in\ker G\), positive semidefiniteness of \(G\) and its definition yield
\[
0=c^{\prime}Gc=E_P[(c^{\prime}t)^2].
\tag{3}
\]
Hence \(c^{\prime}t=0\) in \(L_2(P)\).  Since \(D\) is a well-defined linear functional on \(\mathcal S_{J_n,P}\), Definition \(\ref{def:gap-one-step}\) gives
\[
c^{\prime}g
=\sum_{j=1}^{J_n}c_jD[t_j]
=D[c^{\prime}t]
=D[0]
=0.
\tag{4}
\]
Thus \(g\in(\ker G)^{\perp}\).  The matrix \(G\) is finite-dimensional and symmetric, so
\[
(\ker G)^{\perp}=\operatorname{range}(G),
\qquad GG^{\dagger}g=g.
\tag{5}
\]

Set \(a=G^{\dagger}g\) and \(\zeta=t^{\prime}a\).  Definition \(\ref{def:gap-one-step}\) identifies this \(\zeta\) with \(\zeta_{\Delta,J_n,P}\).  Equation (2) gives \(\zeta\in\mathcal S_{J_n,P}\subseteq\mathcal T_P\).  For an arbitrary \(s=c^{\prime}t\in\mathcal S_{J_n,P}\), symmetry of \(G^{\dagger}\), (5), and linearity of \(D\) give
\[
\begin{aligned}
E_P[\zeta s]
&=a^{\prime}Gc
=g^{\prime}G^{\dagger}Gc
=g^{\prime}c
=\sum_{j=1}^{J_n}c_jD[t_j]
=D[s].
\end{aligned}
\tag{6}
\]
For the third equality, \(G^{\dagger}G\) is the orthogonal projector onto \(\operatorname{range}(G)\), and (5) places \(g\) in that range.

If \(\widetilde\zeta\in\mathcal S_{J_n,P}\) is another representer, then (6) applied to \(s=\widetilde\zeta-\zeta\) for both representers yields
\[
E_P[(\widetilde\zeta-\zeta)^2]=0.
\tag{7}
\]
Thus the representer is unique as an element of \(L_2(P)\), even when \(G\) is singular.  Finally, using (5) and the Moore--Penrose identity \(G^{\dagger}GG^{\dagger}=G^{\dagger}\),
\[
E_P[\zeta^2]
=a^{\prime}Ga
=g^{\prime}G^{\dagger}GG^{\dagger}g
=g^{\prime}G^{\dagger}g.
\tag{8}
\]
Equations (1)--(8) prove every population assertion.  They do not control the difference between the estimated and population derivative vectors, Gram inverses, or Riesz representers; accordingly, no sample expansion or Wald conclusion is drawn.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
Let \(P\) be an interior law covered by Lemma \(\ref{lem:complete-normal-tangent-projection}\).  Fix \(n\), and suppose that the observable directional derivative \(D\Delta_{\mathrm{cmp},P}\) used in Definition \(\ref{def:gap-one-step}\) is a well-defined linear functional on
\[
\mathcal S_{J_n,P}=\{c^{\prime}t_{J_n,P}:c\in\mathbb R^{J_n}\}\subset L_2^0(P).
\]
Then every coordinate \(t_{j,P}\) belongs to \(\mathcal T_P\), the derivative vector satisfies
\[
g_{\Delta,J_n,P}\in\operatorname{range}(G_{J_n,P}),
\]
and
\[
\zeta_{\Delta,J_n,P}
=t_{J_n,P}^{\prime}G_{J_n,P}^{\dagger}g_{\Delta,J_n,P}
\in\mathcal S_{J_n,P}\subseteq\mathcal T_P
\]
is the unique element of \(\mathcal S_{J_n,P}\) satisfying
\[
E_P[\zeta_{\Delta,J_n,P}s]
=D\Delta_{\mathrm{cmp},P}[s]
\qquad\text{for every }s\in\mathcal S_{J_n,P}.
\]
Moreover,
\[
E_P[\zeta_{\Delta,J_n,P}^2]
=g_{\Delta,J_n,P}^{\prime}G_{J_n,P}^{\dagger}g_{\Delta,J_n,P}.
\]
Thus projection against the complete period-specific normal vector removes the former population tangent-space obstruction.  This is only a population finite-sieve characterization: it makes no asymptotic-linearity, variance-consistency, or Wald-coverage claim for \(\widehat\Delta_{\mathrm{cmp}}\).
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The current negative claim is false after Definition \(\ref{def:gap-one-step}\) was repaired to project every dictionary coordinate against the complete period-specific normal vector.  Lemma \(\ref{lem:complete-normal-tangent-projection}\) now implies \(t_{j,P}\in\mathcal T_P\) for every coordinate, while the obsolete aggregate-only counterexample is already carried by Theorem \(\ref{thm:frozen-aggregate-sieve-failure}\).  The proposed statement retains exactly the population finite-sieve Riesz result that follows from the repaired core and expressly makes no unproved gap-Wald claim.

proposed.statement:

\]

\]
is the unique element of \(\mathcal S_{J_n,P}\) satisfying

proposed.justification: The repaired complete-normal sieve admits a computable population Riesz representer on every finite score span.
proposed.gap: The result does not establish the derivative-estimation and growing-dimensional Riesz-map remainders needed for asymptotic linearity of \(\widehat\Delta_{\mathrm{cmp}}\).
proposed.consumer: The backend may use this identity to validate population sieve geometry, but it must not expose a gap Wald statistic without a separate asymptotic-linearity theorem.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The narrowed claim uses the complete-normal tangent-projection lemma and the Gram and derivative vectors, so its dependency and free-symbol metadata must replace the stale aggregate-sieve metadata atomically.
